overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the complainant never sought to attend or was refused entry to the July 21 meeting, and the law leaves public comment to the chair's discretion.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged she was denied access to the July 21 open meeting, having been asked by the Superintendent to refrain from entering school buildings.
allegations.key_passage: We cannot, therefore, conclude that she was actually excluded from the Committee’s July 21 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged she was unable to speak publicly during the July 21 meeting, which she said Committee policy allowed for agenda items.
allegations.key_passage: The law does not require that a public body allow public participation, but rather gives the chair of the public body discretion to decide whether to permit public comment during a meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
